title: Stationary Drop Punt
primarySkill: Drop Punt Technique
objective: Develop a technically sound stationary drop punt by teaching correct ball drop, body position, foot contact and follow-through before introducing movement or defensive pressure.
players:
Minimum: 2
Ideal: 10–20
Maximum: Unlimited (working in pairs)
groundSize:
Small Area
Approximately 20 m × 20 m
setup:
Players work in pairs facing each other.
Players should stand:
Under 8–10: 8–10 metres apart.
Under 12–14: 10–15 metres apart.
Under 16 and above: 15–20 metres apart.
Spread pairs evenly across the training area to prevent footballs crossing into neighbouring groups.
howTheDrillWorks:
Player A begins with the football.
Player A performs a stationary drop punt to Player B.
Player B marks or gathers the football.
Player B resets before returning the kick.
Continue for the nominated time.
Swap the preferred kicking foot after several minutes if appropriate.
Players should prioritise correct technique rather than kicking distance.
coachingPoints: Hold the football correctly.
Guide the ball onto the boot rather than throwing it.
Keep their head over the football.
Strike the ball with the laces of the boot.
Finish balanced.
Follow through directly towards the target.
Encourage smooth, controlled kicking rather than maximum power.
whatTheCoachShouldObserve: Provide one coaching correction before allowing several repetitions.

commonErrors.error: Throwing the ball onto the boot
commonErrors.correction: Guide the football gently from the hands.

commonErrors.error: Leaning backwards
commonErrors.correction: Keep the chest over the football.

commonErrors.error: Falling sideways
commonErrors.correction: Finish balanced on the kicking foot.

commonErrors.error: Looking at the target too early
commonErrors.correction: Watch the football until contact.

commonErrors.error: Swinging across the body
commonErrors.correction: Finish with the kicking leg pointing towards the target.

regressions: Allow players to stop and reset after every kick.
Slow the pace of the activity.
Demonstrate the technique again before restarting.
successIndicators: Maintain balance throughout the kicking action.
matchApplication:
The drop punt is the primary kicking technique used throughout Australian Football.
This drill develops the technical foundation required for:
Maintaining possession.
Passing to teammates.
Kicking inside 50.
Defensive exits.
Goal kicking.
General field kicking.
Every advanced kicking drill in the AFCRL builds upon the skills developed in KK-001.

title: Partner Accuracy Challenge
primarySkill: Passing Accuracy
objective: Develop the ability to consistently deliver the football to a teammate's advantage by improving kicking accuracy, control and judgement of kicking weight. Players learn that an effective pass is one that allows the receiver to mark or gather the football with minimal movement.
players:
Minimum: 2
Ideal: 10–20
Maximum: Unlimited (working in pairs)
groundSize:
Small Area
Approximately 20 m × 20 m
setup:
Players work in pairs facing each other.
Players should stand:
Under 8–10: 8–10 metres apart.
Under 12–14: 10–15 metres apart.
Under 16 and above: 15–20 metres apart.
Each pair should have sufficient space to kick safely without interfering with neighbouring groups.
The receiving player should remain stationary throughout the drill.
howTheDrillWorks:
Player A kicks to Player B.
The objective is to deliver the football directly to Player B's chest without requiring them to move their feet.
Player B marks or gathers the football.
Player B immediately returns the kick using the same objective.
Continue for the allocated time.
Coaches may introduce a simple scoring system:
2 points for a chest mark.
1 point if the receiver gathers the football cleanly after one bounce.
0 points if the receiver must move significantly or the football misses the target.
The emphasis should remain on quality rather than competition.
coachingPoints: Look at the target before beginning the kicking action.
Kick to where the receiver can comfortably mark the football.
Match the force of the kick to the required distance.
Maintain the same drop punt technique regardless of distance.
Stay balanced throughout the kicking action.
Finish towards the intended target.
Players should understand that kicking accurately is more important than kicking hard.
coachingCues: "Kick to your teammate, not at them."
whatTheCoachShouldObserve: Whether the receiver is forced to move.
Encourage players to evaluate each kick before receiving coaching feedback.

commonErrors.error: Receiver moving sideways
commonErrors.correction: Finish directly towards the target.

commonErrors.error: Kick travelling too high
commonErrors.correction: Reduce the height of the ball drop and maintain a flatter trajectory.

commonErrors.error: Kick travelling too hard
commonErrors.correction: Reduce leg speed and focus on control.

commonErrors.error: Kick falling short
commonErrors.correction: Complete the follow-through and accelerate through the football.

commonErrors.error: Receiver unable to mark comfortably
commonErrors.correction: Encourage the kicker to visualise the exact landing point before kicking.

regressions: Encourage players to stop and reset after each kick.
successIndicators: Deliver the football directly to the receiver.
Require minimal movement from the receiver.
Demonstrate good judgement of kicking weight.
Improve accuracy over the duration of the drill.
matchApplication: Most possessions in Australian Football involve passing to a teammate under little or no pressure. This drill develops the fundamental ability to consistently hit a teammate's preferred side, allowing the next possession to be completed quickly and efficiently.

title: Kick and Follow
primarySkill: Kicking While Moving
objective: Teach players to move immediately after disposing of the football rather than remaining stationary. Players kick to a teammate, follow their kick and rotate continuously through the drill.
groundSize:
Small to Medium Area
Approximately 25 m × 15 m per group
setup:
Create two lines facing each other.
Place one cone at the front of each line.
Recommended distance between lines:
Under 8–10: 10 metres.
Under 12–14: 15 metres.
Under 16 and above: 20 metres.
Place a second cone approximately three metres behind each front cone to organise the waiting players.
The football begins with the first player in one line.
howTheDrillWorks:
Player A kicks to Player B at the opposite line.
Player A immediately follows the kick by running to the back of Player B’s line.
Player B marks or gathers the football.
Player B resets and kicks to the next player in the opposite line.
Player B follows the kick to the back of that line.
The drill continues in a continuous pattern.
Players should communicate the intended target before kicking.
coachingPoints: Prepare the football before reaching the kicking point.
Kick accurately to the receiver’s advantage.
Move immediately after disposal.
Run past the receiver rather than stopping in the middle.
Communicate early.
Maintain appropriate spacing in the lines.
The drill should flow continuously without players standing in the kicking lane.
whatTheCoachShouldObserve: Whether players move immediately after disposal.
Players crossing through the kicking lane.
If lines become long, create additional groups.

commonErrors.error: Player watches the kick and remains stationary
commonErrors.correction: Run immediately after the football leaves the boot.

commonErrors.error: Players collide in the middle
commonErrors.correction: Follow the kick outside the main kicking lane.

commonErrors.error: Receiver is not ready
commonErrors.correction: Demand early voice and eye contact.

commonErrors.error: Kicks become rushed
commonErrors.correction: Require players to balance before kicking.

commonErrors.error: Long waiting lines
commonErrors.correction: Divide players into smaller groups.

progressions: Require players to use the non-preferred foot.
Add a short lead before receiving.
Add a handball before the kick.
regressions: Allow players to walk after kicking.
Remove the follow run until kicking accuracy improves.
Use a stationary partner drill first.
matchApplication:
Players must continue working after disposal during a match.
Following the football can create:
A handball receive.
An overlap.
Support at the next contest.
Defensive cover if possession is lost.

title: Moving Target Kicking
primarySkill: Kicking to a Moving Receiver
objective: Teach players to kick accurately to a teammate who is moving rather than standing still. Players learn to place the football into the receiver’s running path so they can mark without slowing down or changing direction.
groundSize:
Medium Area
Approximately 30 m × 20 m
setup:
Create two lines facing each other approximately 20 metres apart.
Place a starting cone five metres to the side of each receiving line.
The first receiver starts at the side cone rather than directly in front of the kicker.
The football begins with the first player in the opposite line.
howTheDrillWorks:
The receiver begins at the side cone.
The receiver leads diagonally into the space between the two lines.
The kicker waits until the receiver begins moving.
The kicker delivers the football in front of the receiver.
The receiver marks while continuing forward.
The receiver carries the football to the opposite line.
The kicker moves to the receiving line.
The drill repeats in the opposite direction.
The lead should begin before the kick is released.
coachingPoints: Communicate before beginning the lead.
Watch the receiver’s movement.
Kick to where the receiver is going.
Place the football slightly in front of the receiver.
Match the weight of the kick to the speed of the lead.
Avoid kicking directly at the receiver’s current position.
The receiver should accelerate into the football rather than waiting underneath it.
whatTheCoachShouldObserve: Timing between the lead and kick.

commonErrors.error: Kick goes behind the receiver
commonErrors.correction: Aim further into the receiver’s running path.

commonErrors.error: Receiver starts too early
commonErrors.correction: Wait until the kicker is balanced and ready.

commonErrors.error: Receiver stops under the football
commonErrors.correction: Kick flatter and further in front.

commonErrors.error: Kicker watches the football instead of the receiver
commonErrors.correction: Scan the receiver before beginning the kicking action.

commonErrors.error: No communication
commonErrors.correction: Require the receiver to call before leading.

progressions: Increase the speed of the lead.
Add a passive defender following the receiver.
regressions: Allow the receiver to walk through the pattern.
Stop and reset after each repetition.
successIndicators: Allow the receiver to maintain speed.
Time the kick with the lead.
Deliver the football at a markable height.
matchApplication:
Players regularly kick to teammates who are leading into space.
Accurate placement allows the receiver to:
Mark without slowing down.
Play on quickly.
Maintain attacking momentum.
Avoid nearby defenders.

title: Short Approach Drop Punt
primarySkill: Drop Punt from a Short Approach
objective: Progress players from stationary kicking to executing a drop punt after a short, controlled approach. Players learn to coordinate their steps, ball preparation and kicking action without rushing.
groundSize:
Small to Medium Area
Approximately 25 m × 20 m
setup:
Players work in pairs facing each other.
Place a starting cone approximately three metres behind each player’s kicking cone.
Recommended kicking distances:
Under 8–10: 8–10 metres.
Under 12–14: 12–15 metres.
Under 16 and above: 15–20 metres.
Players begin at the rear starting cone.
howTheDrillWorks:
Player A begins with the football at the starting cone.
Player A walks or jogs forward for two to four controlled steps.
Player A performs a drop punt from the kicking cone.
Player B marks or gathers the football.
Player B resets at their starting cone.
Player B repeats the short approach and kick.
Continue for the allocated time.
Increase approach speed only when technique remains consistent.
The approach should remain controlled rather than becoming a sprint.
coachingPoints: Prepare the football during the approach.
Keep the final steps controlled.
Maintain balance before contact.
Guide the football onto the boot.
Avoid taking an excessively long final step.
Follow through towards the target.
Continue moving naturally after the kick.
The kicking action should remain similar to the stationary drop punt.
whatTheCoachShouldObserve: Whether the player rushes as speed increases.
Reduce the approach speed if technique deteriorates.

commonErrors.error: Player runs too quickly
commonErrors.correction: Slow the approach and regain control.

commonErrors.error: Ball is prepared too late
commonErrors.correction: Position the football before the final two steps.

commonErrors.error: Final stride is too long
commonErrors.correction: Shorten the final step to keep the body balanced.

commonErrors.error: Player stops before kicking
commonErrors.correction: Maintain smooth forward momentum through the kick.

commonErrors.error: Ball drop moves across the body
commonErrors.correction: Guide the football directly over the kicking foot.

progressions: Progress to a continuous running kick.
Receive a handball before beginning the approach.
regressions: Allow players to rehearse the steps without the football.
successIndicators: Coordinate the approach and kicking action.
matchApplication:
Players rarely kick from a completely stationary position during general play.
This drill introduces the movement coordination required to prepare and execute the football while approaching the point of disposal.

title: Ground Ball Gather and Kick
primarySkill: Kicking After a Ground Ball Gather
objective: Develop the ability to collect a ground ball cleanly, accelerate away from the contest and execute an accurate kick. Players learn to secure possession before transitioning quickly into the kicking action.
players: Minimum: 4 Ideal: 8–16 Maximum: 20 using multiple lanes
groundSize:
Medium Area
Approximately 35 m × 20 m
setup:
Create a straight lane.
Place:
A starting cone.
A ground-ball cone five to eight metres ahead.
A kicking cone another five to eight metres ahead.
A receiving cone 15–25 metres beyond the kicking cone.
A feeder stands beside the ground-ball cone.
Players form lines at the starting and receiving cones.
howTheDrillWorks:
Player A runs from the starting cone.
The feeder rolls the football into Player A’s path.
Player A lowers the body and gathers the football cleanly.
Player A accelerates away from the collection point.
Player A prepares the football before reaching the kicking cone.
Player A executes a running drop punt to Player B.
Player B marks or gathers the football.
Player A continues to the receiving line.
Player B returns to the starting line with the football.
Rotate the feeder regularly.
The ground ball should be rolled at a realistic but controllable speed.
coachingPoints: Approach the football with controlled speed.
Lower the hips and keep the head over the ball.
Use two hands whenever possible.
Gather the football cleanly before accelerating.
Take the first steps away from the collection point.
Prepare the football early.
Balance through the running kick.
Players should not attempt to kick before possession is secure.
whatTheCoachShouldObserve: If players repeatedly fumble, reduce the speed of the rolled football.

commonErrors.error: Player bends only at the waist
commonErrors.correction: Lower the hips and bend the knees.

commonErrors.error: Player uses one hand unnecessarily
commonErrors.correction: Gather with two hands whenever space allows.

commonErrors.error: Player looks towards the target before securing the football
commonErrors.correction: Complete the collection before lifting the eyes.

commonErrors.error: Ball preparation is rushed
commonErrors.correction: Accelerate first, then move the football into kicking position.

commonErrors.error: Player kicks while leaning forward excessively
commonErrors.correction: Regain balance during the steps after the gather.

progressions: Increase the speed or angle of the ground ball.
Require the player to change direction after gathering.
Begin with a contested ground ball.
regressions: Allow the player to stop after gathering.
Remove the kicking component until collection improves.
successIndicators: Complete the sequence without unnecessary delay.
matchApplication:
Ground balls regularly begin attacking possessions.
Players must collect cleanly, escape immediate pressure and deliver accurately to a teammate.
This drill applies to:
Loose-ball wins.
Crumbing.
Contested-ball exits.
Defensive rebounds.
Midfield stoppage releases.

title: Contested Gather and Kick
primarySkill: Kicking After Contested Possession
objective: Develop the ability to win or secure a contested ground ball, escape pressure and execute an effective kick. Players learn to place the body between the opponent and the football before creating enough space to dispose accurately.
players: Minimum: 6 Ideal: 10–18 Maximum: 24 using multiple groups
groundSize:
Medium Area
Approximately 35 m × 25 m
setup:
Create:
A feeder position.
A contest area approximately six metres wide.
Two exit gates beyond the contest.
One kicking target 20–30 metres ahead.
Two players begin on opposite sides of the contest area.
The feeder stands five to ten metres away with the football.
howTheDrillWorks:
The feeder rolls or bounces the football into the contest area.
Both players compete to gain possession.
The player who wins the football protects it and exits through either gate.
The opposing player applies controlled pressure without completing a full tackle.
The ball winner accelerates into space.
The ball winner kicks to the target.
Players reset and rotate.
Alternate opponents regularly.
The drill ends if the football becomes trapped for an extended period. Restart with a new feed.
coachingPoints: Approach the football with the body low.
Keep the feet moving.
Position the body between the opponent and the football.
Gather with two hands when possible.
Protect possession.
Exit away from pressure.
Lift the eyes after escaping.
Balance before kicking.
The first objective is to secure possession. The second is to create space for the kick.
whatTheCoachShouldObserve: Stop the drill if contact becomes uncontrolled.

commonErrors.error: Player reaches without using the body
commonErrors.correction: Win position between the opponent and football first.

commonErrors.error: Player stands upright at the contest
commonErrors.correction: Lower the hips and keep the feet moving.

commonErrors.error: Ball winner tries to kick immediately
commonErrors.correction: Exit pressure before preparing the disposal.

commonErrors.error: Player runs directly into the opponent
commonErrors.correction: Use the open gate away from pressure.

commonErrors.error: Kicking technique collapses under pressure
commonErrors.correction: Regain balance after the exit before kicking.

progressions: Require a handball receive before kicking.
Reduce the size of the exit gates.
Allow full tackling for appropriately prepared groups.
regressions: Roll the football directly towards one player.
Allow the ball winner to stop after exiting.
successIndicators: Recover quickly after losing the contest.
matchApplication:
This drill replicates possessions that begin with:
A loose ball.
A stoppage spill.
A marking contest.
A defensive ground ball.
A forward-half turnover.
Players must secure possession before creating a usable disposal.
relatedDrills: KK-022 – Ground Ball Gather and Kick

title: Time-Limited Kick
primarySkill: Quick Kicking Execution
objective: Develop the ability to scan, select a target and execute an accurate kick within a limited period. Players learn to prepare before possession and avoid wasting time once the football is secured.
players: Minimum: 6 Ideal: 10–18 Maximum: 24 using multiple groups
groundSize:
Medium Area
Approximately 35 m × 30 m
setup:
Place one central receiving cone.
Position three targets approximately 20 metres away at different angles.
A feeder stands 10–15 metres from the central receiver.
Players form lines at the feeder, receiver and target positions.
howTheDrillWorks:
The receiver scans the target positions.
The feeder passes the football to the receiver.
As the football arrives, the coach begins a countdown.
The receiver must select and kick to a target within the allowed time.
Recommended time limits:
Under 12: Four seconds.
Under 14: Three seconds.
Under 16 and above: Two to three seconds.
The selected target marks or gathers the football.
Players rotate positions.
Continue for the allocated time.
The coach may nominate that one target is unavailable immediately before possession.
coachingPoints: Scan before receiving.
Know the available targets.
Prepare the football immediately.
Take only the steps required.
Remain calm under the countdown.
Select a simple option.
Maintain technical quality.
The time limit should challenge decision speed without making accurate execution impossible.
whatTheCoachShouldObserve: Adjust the countdown to match player ability.

commonErrors.error: Player waits until possession to scan
commonErrors.correction: Identify targets before the football arrives.

commonErrors.error: Kicker rushes the ball drop
commonErrors.correction: Keep the technique controlled despite the countdown.

commonErrors.error: Player searches for the perfect option
commonErrors.correction: Use the first safe and effective target.

commonErrors.error: Too many steps are taken
commonErrors.correction: Prepare the football immediately after possession.

commonErrors.error: Time limit causes repeated failure
commonErrors.correction: Add one second until players regain confidence.

progressions: Remove one option on the coach’s call.
Require the non-preferred foot for selected targets.
Begin with a ground ball gather.
regressions: Allow the receiver to begin with the football.
matchApplication:
Players often have limited time after:
Taking possession in traffic.
Receiving at half-back.
Winning a clearance.
Marking and playing on.
Collecting a loose football.

title: Forward Entry After Ground Ball
primarySkill: Forward Entry After a Ground Ball Gather
objective: Develop the ability to gather a loose football outside forward 50 and quickly convert possession into an effective forward entry. Players learn to secure the football first, accelerate from the contest and identify the best attacking option.
players: Minimum: 9 Ideal: 12–21 Maximum: 24 using multiple groups
groundSize:
Large Area
Approximately 55 m × 40 m
setup:
Place:
One starting cone 55 metres from goal.
One ground-ball collection zone eight metres ahead.
Three forward starting positions inside 50.
One feeder beside the collection zone.
Players form lines at the starting and forward positions.
howTheDrillWorks:
The attacker runs towards the collection zone.
The feeder rolls the football into the attacker’s path.
The attacker gathers cleanly.
The attacker accelerates away from the collection point.
The forwards begin their leads.
The attacker scans and selects the best option.
The attacker delivers inside 50.
The forward marks or gathers and finishes at goal.
Players rotate through all positions.
Vary the ground-ball angle and forward leads.
The player should not look forward before securing possession.
coachingPoints: Approach under control.
Get low and use two hands.
Secure possession before accelerating.
Take the first steps away from the collection point.
Lift the eyes early after the gather.
Prepare the football during the run.
Select the forward with the best space.
Maintain balance through disposal.
whatTheCoachShouldObserve: Whether the player rushes immediately after gathering.

commonErrors.error: Player looks forward before securing the ball
commonErrors.correction: Complete the gather first.

commonErrors.error: Attacker remains low for too long
commonErrors.correction: Rise and accelerate after possession is secure.

commonErrors.error: Ball preparation begins too late
commonErrors.correction: Move it into kicking position during the exit steps.

commonErrors.error: Player kicks to the first voice heard
commonErrors.correction: Scan all forward options.

commonErrors.error: Technique collapses after a poor gather
commonErrors.correction: Regain balance before disposal.

regressions: Allow the player to stop after gathering.
matchApplication:
This drill applies when players:
Win a loose ball outside forward 50.
Gather a spill from a contest.
Recover a turnover.
Crumb a marking contest.
Attack before the opposition can reset.
relatedDrills: KK-022 – Ground Ball Gather and Kick

title: Forward Entry from Opposite Foot
primarySkill: Non-Preferred Foot Forward Entry
objective: Develop the ability to deliver inside 50 using the non-preferred foot when body position, pressure or field location removes the preferred-side option.
players: Minimum: 8 Ideal: 12–20 Maximum: 24 using multiple groups
groundSize:
Large Area
Approximately 50 m × 40 m
setup:
Place one ball-carrier position outside forward 50.
Create two leading targets positioned so the non-preferred foot provides the more natural kicking angle.
A feeder stands 10–15 metres behind or beside the ball carrier.
Players rotate through feeder, kicker and forward roles.
howTheDrillWorks:
The kicker receives from the feeder.
The forwards begin their leads.
The kicker must use the non-preferred foot.
The kicker selects the better of the two targets.
The kicker delivers to the receiver’s advantage.
The selected forward marks or gathers and finishes at goal.
Players rotate positions.
Repeat from both sides of the ground.
Keep the distance realistic enough for sound technique.
coachingPoints: Hold the football correctly for the non-preferred side.
Guide it directly over the kicking foot.
Maintain balance.
Use a smooth leg swing.
Accept reduced distance.
Select a target within realistic range.
Avoid turning back onto the preferred foot automatically.
Finish towards the target.
whatTheCoachShouldObserve: Willingness to use the non-preferred foot.
Whether players turn back into pressure.

commonErrors.error: Player turns back onto the preferred foot
commonErrors.correction: Commit to the non-preferred-side option.

commonErrors.error: Ball crosses the body
commonErrors.correction: Hold and guide it directly over the kicking foot.

commonErrors.error: Player tries to kick too far
commonErrors.correction: Choose a closer target and prioritise contact.

commonErrors.error: Kicker falls sideways
commonErrors.correction: Slow the approach and finish balanced.

commonErrors.error: Decision is delayed through lack of confidence
commonErrors.correction: Scan early and commit once the option appears.

progressions: Add passive pressure on the preferred side.
regressions: Return to basic non-preferred foot kicking.
matchApplication:
Non-preferred foot forward entries are required when:
Opponents block the preferred side.
Players receive near the boundary.
Body position limits turning.
Fast ball movement demands immediate disposal.
A teammate is open on the opposite angle.

title: Forward Entry Decision Game
primarySkill: Live Forward Entry Decision Making
objective: Develop live forward-entry decisions in a constrained game. Players learn to select between leading targets, space, short possession and deeper options while defenders actively influence the available lanes.
players: Minimum: 12 Ideal: 16–24 Maximum: 30 using two areas
groundSize:
Large Area
Approximately 70 m × 50 m
setup:
Create a playing area extending from approximately 70 metres from goal to the goal line.
Divide players into:
Attacking team.
Defending team.
Optional neutral transition players.
Recommended starting format:
Four to six attackers.
Three to five defenders.
One or two neutral players outside forward 50.
Start each repetition with a neutral player or coach feeding the football to an attacker outside 50.
howTheDrillWorks:
The attacking team gains possession outside forward 50.
Forwards create leads and maintain spacing.
Defenders attempt to deny the most dangerous options.
The ball carrier decides whether to:
Kick to a leading forward.
Kick into space.
Use a short possession.
Switch the angle.
Retain the football.
The attack continues until:
A shot at goal is completed.
The defence wins possession.
The football leaves the area.
Reset and begin a new repetition.
Rotate attackers and defenders regularly.
Award points for decision quality as well as scoring.
Optional scoring:
Three points for a marked kick that creates a shot.
Two points for a forward gathering a kick to advantage.
One point for retaining possession inside 50.
Bonus point for using a non-preferred foot successfully.
coachingPoints: Scan before receiving.
Maintain forward spacing.
Avoid leading into the same area.
Recognise defender numbers.
Use the first strong option.
Avoid low-percentage kicks to outnumbered contests.
Kick to space when appropriate.
Retain possession when no strong entry exists.
Balance risk with scoring potential.
The coach should avoid stopping every repetition. Allow players to experience the consequences of their decisions.
whatTheCoachShouldObserve: Whether players retain possession when required.
Use brief feedback between repetitions rather than constant interruption.

commonErrors.error: Forwards crowd one area
commonErrors.correction: Maintain separate leading lanes and depth.

commonErrors.error: Ball carrier automatically kicks long
commonErrors.correction: Scan short, lateral and space options.

commonErrors.error: Attackers hold the football too long
commonErrors.correction: Use the first strong option before defenders recover.

commonErrors.error: Players force kicks into outnumbers
commonErrors.correction: Retain possession or change the angle.

commonErrors.error: Entries favour defenders
commonErrors.correction: Kick to the forward’s protected side or into open space.

progressions: Add transition after a defensive turnover.
Restrict the number of possessions before entry.
Track entry type and scoring outcome.
regressions: Stop after the first forward entry.
matchApplication:
This drill directly replicates live inside-50 decision making, including:
Fast entries.
Slow entries.
Boundary entries.
Corridor entries.
Kicks to space.
Short possession.
Deep contests.
Entries under pressure.

title: Intercept and Switch
primarySkill: Switching Play After an Intercept
objective: Develop the ability to recognise and execute a switch immediately after winning an intercept possession. Players learn to use the opposition’s movement towards one side to access space on the opposite side.
groundSize:
Large Area
Approximately 65 m × 50 m
setup:
Place:
One feeder on a boundary side.
One intended attacking target.
One intercept player between them.
One short release target centrally.
One wide switch target on the opposite side.
One forward outlet beyond the switch target.
Add one or two recovering defenders.
howTheDrillWorks:
The feeder kicks towards the intended target.
The intercept player marks or wins possession.
The short release and switch target move immediately.
The interceptor may:
Kick directly to the switch.
Use the short release before switching.
The football moves to the opposite side.
The switch target delivers to the forward outlet.
Recovering defenders attempt to close the switch lanes.
Players rotate through all positions.
Repeat from both sides.
The intercept player must decide whether the direct switch is safe.
coachingPoints: Scan the opposite side before completing the intercept.
Recognise where the opposition has shifted.
Use a short release when the direct switch is too difficult.
Maintain wide positioning.
Kick with appropriate distance and trajectory.
Avoid floating the football across the ground.
Move before defensive recovery.
Support after disposal.
coachingCues: “Win it and see the far side.”
whatTheCoachShouldObserve: Accuracy of the final outlet kick.

commonErrors.error: Interceptor automatically kicks down the same side
commonErrors.correction: Scan the opposite side immediately.

commonErrors.error: Direct switch is attempted through pressure
commonErrors.correction: Use the short release first.

commonErrors.error: Wide player moves towards congestion
commonErrors.correction: Hold width until the kick is released.

commonErrors.error: Switch kick hangs in the air
commonErrors.correction: Use a flatter trajectory when possible.

commonErrors.error: Ball movement is too slow
commonErrors.correction: Prepare the next option before receiving.

progressions: Require a long non-preferred foot kick.
Continue into a live forward entry.
regressions: Allow the interceptor to begin with the football.
successIndicators: Choose direct or assisted switch appropriately.
matchApplication:
This drill develops the ability to exploit opposition shape after:
An intercept mark.
A turnover near the boundary.
A defensive spoil.
A pressured forward entry.
A loose-ball win at half-back.

title: Kick-In Decision Game
primarySkill: Live Kick-In Decision Making
objective: Develop live kick-in decisions against an organised defensive structure. Players learn to select between short possession, switching play, playing on and kicking long according to the available space.
groundSize:
Defensive half of the ground
Approximately 80 m × full or reduced width
equipment: Bibs for attacking and defending teams.
setup:
Use the defensive half of the ground.

Kick-in attacking team.
Defending team.

Short pockets.
Central release.
Wide outlets.
High target.
Opposite-side switch.

Use a short option.
Play on.
Switch.
Kick long.
Defenders attempt to intercept or force the football to a low-value area.

The attacking team exits beyond the designated line.
The defence wins possession.
The football leaves the area.

Avoid predetermining the option.
Coordinate receiver movement.

Use the safest effective exit.
Transition immediately if possession changes.

title: Elite Decision-Making Under Pressure
primarySkill: Selecting and Executing the Best Kicking Option Under Pressure
objective: Develop players’ ability to scan, assess risk and execute the highest-value kicking option while under immediate physical and time pressure.
groundSize: Approximately 60 m × 45 m
setup:
Divide players into two teams.
Mark three vertical kicking channels:
Boundary channel.
Central channel.
Opposite-side channel.
Position one target player at the end of each channel.
Assign different point values to each target based on difficulty and tactical value.
Begin each repetition with a contested possession or coach-fed football.
howTheDrillWorks:
A player wins or receives possession under defensive pressure.
The player has a limited period to scan and dispose of the football.
Teammates create short, medium and long options.
The player selects the most appropriate kick based on:
Defensive positioning.
Available space.
Teammate movement.
Turnover risk.
Play continues for three to five disposals.
A turnover immediately changes the direction of play.
Reset after a successful target connection, score or boundary exit.
coachingPoints: Scan before gaining possession.
Identify pressure before looking for distance.
Use the safest attacking option rather than the most ambitious option.
Keep feet active while assessing the field.
Communicate the intended option early.
Understand the consequences of central turnovers.
Balance speed of play with disposal quality.
whatTheCoachShouldObserve: Support movement around the ball carrier.

commonErrors.correction: Encourage scanning before possession arrives.

commonErrors.correction: Require assessment of short and central options first.

commonErrors.correction: Make the decision earlier and commit fully.

commonErrors.error: Support players remain stationary
commonErrors.correction: Demand movement before the ball carrier gains possession.

commonErrors.error: Central kick is forced under pressure
commonErrors.correction: Use width or retain possession when the corridor is closed.

progressions: Require alternating short and long options.

Use the wing and overlap.
Switch before accelerating.

Run forward after disposal.
Use aggressive field positioning.

Kick to the receiver’s advantage.

Mark a safe technical area with adequate spacing between players.
Each player stands with a football and at least two metres of clear space around them.
Players face a cone, line marking, partner or stationary target positioned three to five metres away.
Begin without speed, competition or defensive pressure.
Right-handed players initially place their left foot slightly forward when handballing with the right fist; reverse the stance for the opposite hand.
The coach positions themselves where the support hand, striking fist and ball contact point can be clearly observed.
howTheDrillWorks:
Players begin in an athletic stance with knees slightly flexed, head up and the football supported in front of the body.
On the coach’s instruction, each player forms a compact striking fist with the thumb positioned outside the fingers.
Players place the football on the open supporting hand with the long axis directed towards the target.
The striking fist moves forward from behind the football and contacts its lower rear section.
The supporting hand remains open and stable while the striking arm follows through towards the target.
Players retrieve the football, reset their body position and repeat the action at a controlled tempo.
Complete sets of six to ten repetitions before changing the striking hand.
The coach pauses the group when necessary to demonstrate or correct a common technical fault.
coachingPoints: Hold the football on the open supporting hand rather than gripping it tightly between both hands.
Keep the football in front of the body where the player can see the ball and the intended target.
Form a firm, compact fist with the wrist straight and the thumb safely outside the fingers.
Strike through the lower rear section of the football rather than pushing or carrying it forward.
Keep the supporting hand stable and avoid throwing the football upwards before contact.
Transfer body weight slightly towards the target as the fist moves through the ball.
Finish with the striking fist pointing towards the target.
Prioritise clean contact and legal technique before speed or distance.
whatTheCoachShouldObserve: Whether players begin with a balanced stance and the football positioned in front of the body.
Whether the supporting hand stays open and underneath the football.
Whether the fist contacts the football rather than the supporting hand.
Whether the football leaves the hand from a clear striking action rather than a throw.
Whether the follow-through travels towards the intended target.
Whether players can repeat the technique without rushing or losing body control.

commonErrors.error: The football is tossed or thrown from the supporting hand.
commonErrors.correction: Keep the supporting hand still and require the fist to create the football’s movement.

commonErrors.error: The fist contacts the side or middle of the football.
commonErrors.correction: Mark or point to the lower rear contact area and slow the action until contact improves.

commonErrors.error: The striking wrist bends on impact.
commonErrors.correction: Form a firmer fist and keep the wrist aligned with the forearm.

commonErrors.error: The player grips the football tightly with both hands.
commonErrors.correction: Rest the football on the open supporting palm with only light finger control.

commonErrors.error: The player stands upright with locked knees.
commonErrors.correction: Adopt a balanced athletic stance with soft knees and a slight forward weight transfer.

commonErrors.error: The follow-through finishes across the body.
commonErrors.correction: Direct the fist straight through the football and towards the target.

progressions: Handball towards a partner or stationary target from four to six metres.
Complete consecutive repetitions without pausing between each handball.
Alternate the striking hand after every repetition.
Require players to nominate the target before beginning the action.
regressions: Practise the fist movement without a football.
Hold the football closer to the striking fist to reduce the length of the action.
Use a larger soft football or reduced distance for younger players.
Allow the coach or partner to hold the football lightly while the player practises clean contact.
successIndicators: Support the football on an open and stable hand.
Make clear fist-to-football contact without throwing the ball.
Direct the football towards the intended target.
Demonstrate the basic action with both hands at a controlled speed.
matchApplication: A legal and technically sound handball is the foundation of releasing a teammate, maintaining possession and moving the football through congestion. Players who establish correct supporting-hand position, contact and follow-through are better prepared to execute under movement and pressure later in the chapter.

title: Contact Point and Follow-Through
primarySkill: Clean striking contact and directional follow-through
objective: Develop clean contact on the lower rear section of the football and a straight follow-through that produces controlled, accurate ball flight.
groundSize: Pairs positioned four metres apart within a 15-metre × 15-metre technical area.
equipment: Optional removable ball markers or tape
coachingDifficulty: 2 – Basic coaching knowledge and one main teaching focus
setup:
Organise players in pairs facing each other four metres apart.
Place one cone beside each player to maintain the correct distance.
One player begins with the football while the partner presents both hands as a target.
Players use a controlled stationary stance.
The coach identifies the lower rear striking area of the football before the drill begins.
Pairs complete separate blocks with the right and left fist.
howTheDrillWorks:
The player with the football establishes a stable support-hand platform.
The player forms a closed fist with a straight wrist and positions it behind the football.
The fist travels directly through the lower rear section of the football.
The player completes the action with the fist pointing towards the partner’s chest.
The receiver secures the football, briefly checks the previous handball’s flight and returns it using the same technique.
Partners complete eight handballs each with one fist.
Players then change the supporting and striking hands for a second set.
The pair counts clean handballs that travel directly to the partner without excessive loop, wobble or sideways rotation.
coachingPoints: Keep the striking fist compact, with the thumb outside the fingers.
Align the wrist with the forearm before and during contact.
Contact the lower rear section of the football to produce forward flight.
Drive through the football rather than stopping the fist at impact.
Follow through directly towards the partner’s chest.
Use a small forward weight transfer rather than leaning backwards.
Maintain a stable supporting hand until the football has left the platform.
Judge quality by clean flight and accuracy, not by how hard the football is struck.
whatTheCoachShouldObserve: Whether the fist is correctly formed before the action begins.
Whether the wrist remains straight at the point of contact.
Whether contact occurs on the football rather than the support hand.
Whether the football travels with controlled forward rotation rather than excessive wobble.
Whether the follow-through finishes towards the partner.
Whether players maintain the same mechanics with both fists.

commonErrors.error: The fist strikes the middle or top of the football.
commonErrors.correction: Lower the contact point and rehearse the fist path slowly.

commonErrors.error: The wrist bends or turns at impact.
commonErrors.correction: Reset the fist and align the wrist directly behind the football.

commonErrors.error: The action stops immediately after contact.
commonErrors.correction: Extend the fist towards the partner and complete the follow-through.

commonErrors.error: The football floats excessively upwards.
commonErrors.correction: Strike through the lower rear rather than underneath the ball.

commonErrors.error: The football travels across the partner’s body.
commonErrors.correction: Align the platform, fist path and follow-through with the centre of the target.

commonErrors.error: The player tries to create power only with the arm.
commonErrors.correction: Add a controlled weight transfer towards the target.

progressions: Increase the partner distance to five or six metres.
Handball through a one-metre-wide cone gate before reaching the receiver.
Complete five consecutive accurate handballs without resetting the count.
regressions: Reduce the distance to two or three metres.
Use a larger chest-level target such as a handball board.
Pause with the fist positioned behind the football before striking.
Practise the follow-through without a football.
successIndicators: Contact the lower rear section of the football.
Produce controlled and direct ball flight.
Perform the action effectively with both fists.
matchApplication: Clean contact and directional follow-through allow players to release teammates accurately at short and medium distances. This is essential when handballing through congestion, feeding a runner or maintaining possession after winning the football at ground level.

title: Receive at Speed and Release Forward
Boundary Throw-In Fold-Out Handball
primarySkill: Using layered support to exit a boundary throw-in
objective: Develop a boundary-stoppage exit in which midfielders fold away from the contest and use handball to move the football from the boundary into open space.
groundSize: A boundary stoppage area approximately 20 metres × 18 metres with an inside exit lane.
coachingDifficulty: 5 – Expert stoppage structure and contact management
setup:
Mark a boundary line and stoppage zone.
Position one first-possession player near the boundary side of the contest.
Place one fold-out support player two to three metres inside.
Position one wider release runner further infield.
Add two controlled-pressure opponents.
Place a finishing receiver 15 metres infield.
The coach feeds the football from a boundary throw-in simulation.
Mirror the activity on both boundaries.
howTheDrillWorks:
The coach throws or feeds the football into the stoppage.
The first-possession player secures the football near the boundary.
The fold-out support player moves laterally and slightly backwards into clear space.
The first-possession player protects the football and handballs to the fold-out player.
The wider runner accelerates infield.
The fold-out player receives facing the centre of the ground.
The second handball releases the wider runner.
The runner connects with the finishing receiver.
Pressure players attempt to close the inside exit without exceeding contact restrictions.
Rotate roles and repeat from the opposite boundary.
coachingPoints: The boundary-side player must recognise the reduced space.
Fold-out support should move away from the contest, not towards it.
The first handball should be short and protected.
The fold-out player should receive with vision towards the centre.
Wider support must remain separated from the stoppage.
Use the hand that directs the football away from boundary pressure.
The second handball should lead the runner infield.
Players must avoid forcing the exit when the lane is closed.
whatTheCoachShouldObserve: Whether the first-possession player protects the football.
Whether fold-out support creates genuine separation.
Whether the first handball remains short and controlled.
Whether the second receiver holds infield width.
Whether body orientation supports the infield release.
Whether the football exits the stoppage in possession.
Whether the pattern works from both boundaries.

commonErrors.error: Fold-out support moves back into congestion.
commonErrors.correction: Move laterally and backwards into clear infield space.

commonErrors.error: The first-possession player handballs along the boundary.
commonErrors.correction: Use the infield support angle when available.

commonErrors.error: The fold-out receiver faces the boundary.
commonErrors.correction: Open the hips towards the centre before receiving.

commonErrors.error: Wider support starts too close to the stoppage.
commonErrors.correction: Hold separation until the first handball is completed.

commonErrors.error: The second handball forces the receiver sideways.
commonErrors.correction: Lead the runner towards the centre.

commonErrors.error: The exit is attempted through a closed lane.
commonErrors.correction: Retain possession or use an alternate support option.

progressions: Begin from a live boundary throw-in.
Allow the first-possession player to choose between two fold-out options.
Require a forward kick after the exit.
Progress to match-like contact for suitable groups.
successIndicators: Protect and release the first possession.
Exit the stoppage in controlled possession.
matchApplication: Boundary stoppages compress available space. Folding one player away from the contest creates a short outlet and can shift the football into the centre before opposition pressure resets.

title: Wing Fold and Inside Return
primarySkill: Using a wing fold and inside return handball to change the running lane
objective: Develop a wing possession pattern in which the outside player releases an inside runner and receives the football back beyond pressure.
groundSize: A wing corridor approximately 30 metres long and 15 metres wide.
coachingDifficulty: 4 – Advanced support timing and lane management
setup:
Player A begins wide with the football.
Player B begins inside and slightly behind.
Player C starts further forward in the wide lane.
Add one shadow defender between Player A and Player C.
Mark an inside support channel and outside return channel.
Player A must use Player B before regaining possession outside.
Mirror the pattern on both wings.
howTheDrillWorks:
Player A carries forward in the wide lane.
Player B accelerates from inside and behind.
Player A handballs to Player B.
Player A immediately folds behind and then outside Player B.
Player B receives and engages the shadow defender.
Player B returns the football into Player A’s outside run.
Player A receives beyond the defender and handballs to Player C.
Players follow their disposal and rotate.
Repeat on both wings.
Increase tempo only when running lines remain separate.
coachingPoints: Inside support should arrive from behind the ball carrier.
The first handball must be short and accurate.
The original ball carrier should fold behind before moving outside.
Player B should engage the defender before returning the football.
The return handball must lead Player A into the outside lane.
Running lines should remain clearly separated.
Use the correct hand for each direction.
Continue forward after breaking the pressure line.
whatTheCoachShouldObserve: Whether Player B times the inside support run.
Whether Player A folds behind rather than crossing in front.
Whether Player B draws the defender.
Whether the return handball leads the outside runner.
Whether the final connection remains accurate.
Whether both wings are used effectively.

commonErrors.error: Player B begins ahead of the ball carrier.
commonErrors.correction: Start slightly behind and accelerate into the inside lane.

commonErrors.error: Player A crosses in front of Player B.
commonErrors.correction: Fold behind before moving into the outside lane.

commonErrors.error: Player B returns the football immediately.
commonErrors.correction: Carry until the defender commits.

commonErrors.error: The return handball goes behind Player A.
commonErrors.correction: Release earlier and target the outside running path.

commonErrors.error: Players collide or occupy the same line.
commonErrors.correction: Use the marked inside and outside channels.

commonErrors.error: The pattern slows after the return handball.
commonErrors.correction: Accelerate beyond the defender and connect forward.

progressions: Allow Player B to choose between returning outside and continuing inside.
successIndicators: Fold behind into the outside lane.
Draw the defender before the return.
matchApplication: Wing players can use an inside teammate to draw pressure and regain possession outside. The fold-and-return pattern creates overlap while maintaining width and forward momentum.

title: No-Look Support Handball Decision
primarySkill: Using pre-possession scanning to release support without prolonged visual confirmation
objective: Develop the ability to scan support before possession arrives and complete a rapid handball based on confirmed movement and communication rather than staring at the final target.
groundSize: Stations approximately 14 metres long and ten metres wide.
setup:
Organise groups of four: feeder, receiver-ball carrier and two support players.
The receiver-ball carrier begins facing the feeder.
Support players stand behind and to either side of the receiver.
Before the feed, only one support player moves into the active lane.
The receiver must scan over both shoulders before the football arrives.
One shadow defender may stand in front to restrict prolonged turning.
Rotate roles regularly.
howTheDrillWorks:
Both support players begin in their starting positions.
The receiver scans over each shoulder.
One support player moves into space and calls.
The feeder delivers the football to the receiver.
The receiver secures possession while facing the feeder.
Using the earlier scan and communication, the receiver organises the football and handballs to the active support player.
The player may use a brief peripheral check but should not complete a full turn before release.
The support player catches and exits through a gate.
One point is awarded for the correct option and accurate delivery.
Rotate roles after four repetitions.
coachingPoints: Scan both shoulders before the football arrives.
Confirm the support player’s movement and voice.
Secure the football cleanly before release.
Maintain awareness of pressure in front.
Use peripheral vision rather than blindly disposing.
Select the hand aligned with the known support side.
Keep the release compact and legal.
This is an awareness drill, not permission to handball without reliable information.
whatTheCoachShouldObserve: Whether the receiver scans before the feed.
Whether the active support player communicates.
Whether the correct target is selected.
Whether the receiver uses enough visual confirmation to avoid blind disposal.

commonErrors.error: The receiver does not scan before possession.
commonErrors.correction: The feeder must wait for two visible shoulder checks.

commonErrors.error: The player handballs blindly based only on a voice.
commonErrors.correction: Require prior visual confirmation and a brief peripheral check.

commonErrors.error: The receiver turns fully and delays release.
commonErrors.correction: Use the pre-possession scan to organise the handball sooner.

commonErrors.error: The incorrect support player is selected.
commonErrors.correction: Identify colour, position and voice before the football arrives.

commonErrors.error: The handball is rushed before possession is secure.
commonErrors.correction: Complete clean two-hand control before disposal.

commonErrors.error: Players use the drill as a trick rather than an awareness task.
commonErrors.correction: Reinforce that reliable information must exist before release.

progressions: Add a second moving support option.
Delay the support movement until immediately before the feed.
Require release within one second of possession.
Begin with an imperfect handball feed.
regressions: Allow the receiver to turn partially.
successIndicators: Confirm the option through communication or peripheral vision.
matchApplication: Elite players scan before receiving so they can release rapidly when pressure arrives. The skill depends on accurate prior information and communication, not on disposing without awareness.
relatedDrills: HB-035 – Handball Square with Moving Choice

title: Elite Handball Decision and Execution Assessment
Fatigued Stoppage Repeat Scenario
primarySkill: Executing repeated stoppage handball exits under fatigue
objective: Develop the ability to maintain stoppage role discipline, legal handball technique and decision quality across repeated high-intensity contest efforts.
groundSize: A stoppage area approximately 25 metres × 25 metres with two exit corridors.
coachingDifficulty: 5 – Expert workload, stoppage and contact management
setup:
Divide players into two midfield groups.
Mark a central stoppage circle and two exit corridors.
Begin with a live or controlled ball-up.
Each repetition lasts until a clean exit or turnover.
Players immediately complete a short recovery run and return for the next stoppage.
Roles rotate between first possession, close support, outside release and pressure.
Work in blocks of four to six stoppages.
Provide planned recovery between blocks.
howTheDrillWorks:
The coach initiates the first stoppage.
Players contest for possession.
The winning team attempts to complete a handball exit through either corridor.
The opposition applies match-like pressure.
When the repetition ends, players complete the nominated recovery run.
Teams immediately reorganise for the next stoppage.
Repeat four to six times within the block.
Record successful exits, illegal disposals and role errors.
Provide recovery and one technical correction.
Repeat the block with changed roles or exit conditions.
coachingPoints: Re-establish roles before every stoppage.
Fatigue must not remove first-, second- and third-possession structure.
Protect the football before releasing.
Use short, direct handballs in congestion.
Outside support must continue to hold width.
Maintain legal technique when breathing and heart rate are elevated.
Recovery running should not prevent safe contest preparation.
End the block if technique or contact standards deteriorate.
whatTheCoachShouldObserve: Whether roles are reorganised between repetitions.
Whether players default to the dominant-hand side.
Whether players apply the correction in the next block.

commonErrors.error: Players fail to reorganise before the next stoppage.
commonErrors.correction: Assign roles during the recovery run.

commonErrors.error: Handballs become throws under fatigue.
commonErrors.correction: Stop the block and restore the legal support platform and strike.

commonErrors.error: All players move towards the contest.
commonErrors.correction: Maintain outside and behind-ball roles.

commonErrors.error: First-possession players release without protecting the football.
commonErrors.correction: Secure and position the body before disposal.

commonErrors.error: Recovery running creates unsafe contact preparation.
commonErrors.correction: Reduce the running demand or increase reset time.

commonErrors.error: Players repeat the same error across the block.
commonErrors.correction: Provide one specific correction before restarting.

progressions: Require exits through a called side.
regressions: Reduce the number of repetitions per block.
matchApplication: Repeated stoppages late in quarters demand technical and tactical consistency under fatigue. Teams must continue to organise roles and execute legally even after multiple contest efforts.

title: Kick-In Play-On Handball Escape
primarySkill: Using a play-on handball to escape pressure after a kick-in
objective: Develop a coordinated kick-in option in which the player bringing the football into play recognises pressure, plays on legally and releases a supporting teammate by handball.
groundSize: A defensive goal-square and kick-in area approximately 30 metres long and 25 metres wide.
coachingDifficulty: 5 – Expert kick-in, field-position and pressure management
setup:
Position the kick-in player inside the goal square.
Place one short support player towards the boundary pocket.
Position one player behind and outside the initial support.
Place one wider receiver beyond the first pressure line.
Add two defenders who guard the short kick and begin closing once the kick-in player plays on.
Mark a prohibited central turnover zone.
The kick-in player must clearly leave the goal square before handballing.
Mirror the structure on both sides of the ground.
howTheDrillWorks:
The coach signals that the kick-in may begin.
The kick-in player scans the short kicking options and defensive structure.
If the short kick is closed, the player leaves the goal square and plays on.
The nearest support player moves into a visible handball lane.
The kick-in player handballs to the receiver’s protected side.
The receiver continues towards the boundary-side exit.
A second handball releases the wider runner beyond the first defensive line.
Defenders attempt to pressure, tackle or intercept under controlled rules.
The repetition ends after a clean defensive exit or turnover.
Players rotate through kick-in, support, receiver and defensive roles.
coachingPoints: The kick-in player must scan before leaving the goal square.
Playing on should create a better angle rather than simply invite pressure.
The first support option should remain clear of the direct central turnover zone.
Receivers must present before the ball carrier reaches tackling pressure.
Place the football on the receiver’s protected side.
Use firm, direct handballs in the defensive area.
Maintain support behind the football after the first release.
Do not use the handball option when the short kick or safe long kick is clearly superior.
whatTheCoachShouldObserve: Whether the kick-in player scans before playing on.
Whether the player legally exits the goal square.
Whether short support appears at a safe angle.
Whether the first handball avoids the dangerous central zone.
Whether the receiver is protected through placement.
Whether players recognise when handball is not the best option.

commonErrors.error: The player plays on without checking the pressure structure.
commonErrors.correction: Scan short, wide and central defensive positions before leaving the square.

commonErrors.error: The handball is released before the player exits the goal square.
commonErrors.correction: Cross the goal-square line clearly before disposing by hand.

commonErrors.error: Support stands directly in front of goal.
commonErrors.correction: Move towards a safer angled or boundary-side lane.

commonErrors.error: The receiver is given the football on the defender’s side.
commonErrors.correction: Target the protected hand and outside shoulder.

commonErrors.error: The kick-in player runs directly into pressure.
commonErrors.correction: Change the play-on angle or retain the original disposal option.

commonErrors.error: Players force the handball when a safer kick is available.
commonErrors.correction: Use handball only when it creates a genuine defensive escape.

progressions: Allow defenders to change the protected side late.
Reduce the width of the exit lane.
Add an immediate turnover shot on goal.
Allow live kick-or-handball choice from the kick-in.
regressions: Allow the kick-in player more time.
Rehearse the legal play-on movement without pressure.
successIndicators: Create and use a safe support angle.
Exit the defensive area in possession.
matchApplication: A kick-in player may use play-on and handball to escape a closed kicking structure, but the decision carries significant turnover risk near goal. Correct timing, legal movement and safe support angles are essential.

title: Defensive Switch Breakdown Recovery
primarySkill: Recovering possession structure after a planned defensive switch is closed
objective: Develop the ability to abandon a closed defensive switch, retain possession and create an alternate handball exit without panicking or forcing the original plan.
groundSize: A defensive-half area approximately 35 metres × 30 metres.
setup:
Begin with the football in one defensive pocket.
Position two players to form a planned handball switch across the defensive area.
Add defenders who initially allow the first release but close the intended second lane.
Position one emergency support player behind the football.
Mark one alternate boundary-side exit and one prohibited central turnover zone.
The possession team must identify when the switch has broken down.
Rotate all roles regularly.
howTheDrillWorks:
The first defender begins the planned switch with a short handball.
The receiving player turns towards the expected second option.
Defenders close that planned lane.
The ball carrier recognises that the switch is no longer safe.
The player protects possession and uses emergency support behind or outside.
The football is redirected towards the alternate exit.
The team attempts to leave defensive 50 in possession.
Defenders attempt to force a central turnover.
The repetition ends after a clean exit, turnover or football leaving the area.
Reset with different defenders closing the switch at different moments.
coachingPoints: Planned movement must remain adaptable.
Scan the second lane before completing the first handball.
The receiver should not automatically continue the switch.
Maintain support behind the football throughout the pattern.
Protect possession when the lane closes.
Use a firm reset handball to change the angle.
Avoid turning blindly towards defensive goal.
Communicate that the original switch is closed.
whatTheCoachShouldObserve: Whether the initial receiver scans before continuing.
Whether the closed switch is recognised.
Whether the football is protected during the reset.
Whether players avoid the dangerous central zone.
Whether communication changes the team’s movement.
Whether the alternate exit is attacked after the reset.

commonErrors.error: The player continues the switch into a closed lane.
commonErrors.correction: Scan the intended receiver and defender before releasing.

commonErrors.error: Emergency support moves ahead and becomes unavailable.
commonErrors.correction: Remain behind the football until the switch is complete.

commonErrors.error: The receiver turns blindly towards goal.
commonErrors.correction: Keep vision across the defensive area and use controlled footwork.

commonErrors.error: The reset handball is slow and looping.
commonErrors.correction: Use a firm, direct disposal to the supporting player.

commonErrors.error: Teammates continue the original pattern after it closes.
commonErrors.correction: Communicate the reset and move towards the alternate exit.

commonErrors.error: Players become overly cautious after the reset.
commonErrors.correction: Accelerate once the alternate lane is established.

progressions: Allow defenders to choose when the switch closes.
Add a turnover shot on goal.
Allow live kick-or-handball exit after the reset.
regressions: Pause after the lane closes for tactical organisation.
successIndicators: Create and attack a new exit angle.
matchApplication: Planned defensive switches do not always remain available. Teams must recognise when the opposition has closed the pattern and reset safely rather than forcing possession near goal.

title: Forward-Half Counter-Press Retention
primarySkill: Retaining possession in the forward half after winning the football during a counter-press
objective: Develop the ability to secure a forward-half turnover, resist the urge to rush possession and use handball support to create a controlled scoring opportunity.
groundSize: A forward-half area approximately 35 metres × 30 metres.
coachingDifficulty: 5 – Expert counter-press, scoring and turnover management
setup:
Divide players into attacking and defending teams.
Begin with the defending team attempting to exit the forward half.
The attacking team applies a coordinated counter-press.
Mark one central scoring corridor and two reset lanes.
When the attacking team wins possession, it has eight seconds to create a shot or controlled scoring entry.
A minimum of one handball is required after the turnover.
A second turnover allows the defending team to counterattack through an exit gate.
howTheDrillWorks:
The defending team begins attempting to exit.
The attacking team applies pressure and attempts to win possession.
On turnover, the new ball carrier secures and protects the football.
Nearby teammates create short, outside and reset options.
The first handball moves the football away from the turnover pressure.
The team assesses whether the scoring lane is open.
If open, the next possession attacks goal.
If closed, the team retains through a reset lane before re-entering.
A turnover creates an immediate defensive exit.
Play continues in repeated short scenarios.
coachingPoints: The turnover winner must secure possession before attacking.
Nearby support should separate rather than crowd the contest.
The first handball should improve the scoring position.
Avoid handballing directly to a teammate surrounded by defenders.
Use a reset when the immediate scoring lane is closed.
Protect receivers through accurate placement.
Maintain urgency without forcing a low-quality possession.
React immediately if the opposition wins the football back.
whatTheCoachShouldObserve: Whether the turnover winner controls possession.
Whether support separates from the contest.
Whether the first handball improves the attacking angle.
Whether players recognise an open or closed scoring lane.
Whether defensive reaction follows a second turnover.

commonErrors.error: The turnover winner disposes before controlling possession.
commonErrors.correction: Secure the football and scan the scoring structure first.

commonErrors.error: Teammates crowd the turnover point.
commonErrors.correction: Create short, outside and reset support at different angles.

commonErrors.error: The first handball goes to a teammate under equal pressure.
commonErrors.correction: Use the player positioned away from the immediate contest.

commonErrors.error: The team forces the scoring lane.
commonErrors.correction: Reset and change the angle when central pressure is organised.

commonErrors.error: Players lose urgency after using the reset.
commonErrors.correction: Re-attack quickly once the defence shifts.

commonErrors.error: The attacking team stops after losing possession.
commonErrors.correction: Apply immediate counter-pressure or defend the exit gate.

progressions: Award double points for a score created within three possessions.
successIndicators: Recognise open and closed scoring lanes.
matchApplication: Forward-half turnovers create strong scoring opportunities, but rushed disposal can waste the advantage. A controlled first handball can escape the pressure point and create a higher-quality shot.
relatedDrills: HB-059 – Turnover Contest and Handball Counterattack

title: Strong-Wind Low-Trajectory Handball Scenario
primarySkill: Executing low, direct handballs in strong-wind conditions
objective: Develop handball technique and support structure appropriate to strong wind, where high or floating disposals become less reliable.
groundSize: A rectangular area approximately 25 metres × 18 metres, aligned both with and across the prevailing wind.
equipment: Wind indicators or flags where available
setup:
Mark two possession grids:
One aligned with the wind.
One running across the wind.
Divide players into small teams.
Limit handball distance to approximately five metres.
Add one or two shadow defenders.
Mark low target gates between waist and chest height using poles or partner targets.
High, floating handballs do not count towards the possession target.
Rotate groups between wind directions.
howTheDrillWorks:
The possession team begins with the football.
Players create close support at short angles.
Ball carriers deliver low, firm handballs.
Receivers present two hands and adjust for wind movement.
The team scores after five consecutive legal handballs.
A floating disposal, dropped football or interception resets the count.
Defenders pressure and attempt controlled interceptions.
After each round, groups change orientation to the wind.
Coaches compare required force and trajectory.
Play continues in short blocks with technical review.
coachingPoints: Keep support distances shorter in strong wind.
Use a firm, direct striking action.
Avoid high handballs unless no direct lane exists.
Present both hands and expect late football movement.
Keep the support platform stable.
Adjust force when handballing with, against or across the wind.
Protect the football before release.
Prioritise possession quality over disposal distance.
whatTheCoachShouldObserve: Whether ball flight remains low and direct.
Whether force changes with wind direction.
Whether high-risk floating disposals are avoided.
Whether players apply learning after changing orientation.

commonErrors.error: Players use normal dry, calm-condition force.
commonErrors.correction: Adjust striking force according to the wind direction.

commonErrors.error: Handballs float and drift.
commonErrors.correction: Use a lower trajectory and firmer direct strike.

commonErrors.error: Support players remain too far away.
commonErrors.correction: Reduce the distance and create reliable short options.

commonErrors.error: Receivers wait flat-footed.
commonErrors.correction: Stay balanced and adjust late to the football’s movement.

commonErrors.error: Players attempt high handballs over pressure.
commonErrors.correction: Reposition the feet or use a safer support lane.

commonErrors.error: The supporting hand flicks the football in an attempt to add power.
commonErrors.correction: Keep the platform stable and generate force through the fist and body.

progressions: Combine wind with a wet or slippery football where safe.
regressions: Practise stationary handballs in each wind direction.
matchApplication: Strong wind can alter even short football flight. Teams should reduce handball distance, keep disposals direct and create closer support rather than relying on floating releases.

title: Tag-Release Handball System
primarySkill: Using coordinated handball support to release a closely tagged player
objective: Develop a team handball system that helps a closely checked midfielder or playmaker create separation and regain possession in space.
groundSize: A midfield area approximately 25 metres × 20 metres.
coachingDifficulty: 5 – Expert tagging, support and legal-screen management
setup:
Assign one tagged player and one close-checking defender.
Position one primary ball carrier and two support players nearby.
Mark three release lanes through the midfield area.
The tagger maintains close legal body position.
Teammates may create legal running separation but may not block illegally.
The tagged player begins away from the football.
Rotate tagged, supporting and defensive roles.
howTheDrillWorks:
The primary ball carrier receives possession.
The tagged player begins a change-of-direction or run-past movement.
One support player changes angle to force the tagger to navigate traffic legally.
The ball carrier scans whether the tagged player has gained separation.
If free, the ball carrier handballs to the tagged player’s protected side.
The tagged player receives and immediately uses a second support option.
If separation is not created, the ball carrier uses another teammate.
The tagger attempts to maintain position and intercept.
Play continues through the finishing gate.
Rotate roles and vary the release movement.
coachingPoints: The tagged player must change speed and direction purposefully.
Supporting teammates should create legitimate movement, not illegal blocks.
The ball carrier should not force the football to the tagged player.
Place the handball on the side away from the tagger.
The tagged player should release quickly after receiving.
Alternate support must remain available.
Communication should identify whether separation has been created.
The system should help the tagged player without distorting the entire team structure.
whatTheCoachShouldObserve: Whether the tagged player creates genuine movement.
Whether the ball carrier scans the separation.
Whether the handball reaches the protected side.
Whether an alternate option is used when the tag remains effective.
Whether the tagged player releases quickly.
Whether the tagger maintains legal contact.

commonErrors.error: The tagged player runs at one speed.
commonErrors.correction: Use changes of pace and direction to create separation.

commonErrors.error: Supporting players illegally block the tagger.
commonErrors.correction: Use legitimate running lines and maintain legal contact.

commonErrors.error: The ball carrier forces possession to the tagged player.
commonErrors.correction: Use the alternate support option when separation is not created.

commonErrors.error: The handball goes to the tagger’s side.
commonErrors.correction: Target the protected hand and outside shoulder.

commonErrors.error: The tagged player holds the football after receiving.
commonErrors.correction: Use the next support option quickly before the tagger recovers.

commonErrors.error: The entire team crowds around the tagged player.
commonErrors.correction: Maintain broader team spacing and use only the necessary support.

progressions: Require the tagged player to become the third possession.
Introduce a forward entry after the release.
regressions: Keep the tagged player stationary before the lead.
successIndicators: Recognise whether the tagged player is genuinely free.
Protect the receiver through ball placement.
Release the tagged player into space.
matchApplication: Opposition teams may closely tag a key midfielder or playmaker. Coordinated movement and protected-side handball placement can help that player gain separation without forcing possession or using illegal blocks.

title: Handball-to-Kick Transition Decision Game
primarySkill: Recognising when a handball chain should end and transition to a kick
objective: Develop the ability to use handball to create advantage and then select the correct moment to finish the chain with a kick rather than over-handballing.
groundSize: A transition corridor approximately 40 metres long and 22 metres wide.
setup:
Position four to six attackers through the transition corridor.
Add two to four defenders in staggered positions.
Begin with the football in the rear half of the corridor.
Mark three possible kicking zones.
Attackers may use handball to break pressure.
A kick is required before the final scoring zone.
Defenders attempt to delay, intercept and force over-handballing.
Rotate attacking and defensive roles.
howTheDrillWorks:
The attacking group begins advancing with possession.
Players use handball to create overlap or move around defenders.
The ball carrier scans the kicking zones and forward targets.
Once a player receives in balance with a clear kicking lane, the handball chain should end.
The player kicks to the forward target.
If the kicking lane remains closed, the group may continue handballing.
Defenders attempt to force rushed or unnecessary disposals.
Attackers score for selecting the correct transition point and connecting with the target.
Defenders score for turnovers or forcing the group beyond the final kicking zone.
Reset and rotate roles.
coachingPoints: Handball should create time, space or a better kicking angle.
Do not continue handballing after a balanced player gains a clear forward option.
The receiver should arrive in a position suitable to kick.
Support runners must avoid running past purely to demand another handball.
